text:
maria: Quick Q3 capacity thread — forecasting shows a ~55% YoY increase in hosted API traffic and a short, sharp 4-6 week marketing spike. We need a buy vs lease recommendation for GPUs by EOD Friday. Can ops/finance weigh in? :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alex: Pulled numbers this morning. Two scenarios:
- conservative: +80 GPUs sustained (A100 80GB equiv)
- aggressive: +250 GPUs for a 6-week peak
Rough calc for aggressive:```
peak_gpus = 250
peak_days = 42
gpu_hours = peak_gpus * 24 * peak_days  # 252000
```
That 252k GPU-hours is the incremental run on top of baseline.

noah: Rack/network constraints: we have ~40 free rack U in us-west colo but limited 100G spine ports available. If we buy hardware we need lead time for cross-connects and a 2-week on-site install window. APAC/DC options have longer customs lead times.

kevin: Finance lens: buy vs lease (numbers rough):
- Buy H100-style cards + servers: capex ~ $60k per node (incl chassis/net), depreciation 3y -> ~ $1.7k/month per node.
- Lease (1yr) / dedicated host: op-ex ~ $6-$9k/month per node depending on term and vendor.
- Cloud on-demand H100 ~ $25/hr (too expensive for sustained).
We should compare cost over 6-12 months and include warranty/ops headcount.

sasha: Region ask — our customers in eu-central and ap-southeast are driving the spike. If we centralize capacity in us-west we add ~80ms p90 for APAC; that hurts product SLAs. Prefer some regional presence even if smaller.

alex: Proposal: hybrid approach:
1) Short-term (Q3 ramp): lease 120 nodes in us-west + 40 in eu-central for 12 weeks to cover peak. Fast provisioning, no heavy capex risk.
2) Medium-term (Q4+): purchase 100 nodes spread across us-west + eu to handle baseline growth.
This smooths cashflow and respects lead times.

maria: Ops questions: who owns vendor negotiation? procurement? Also what's the expected utilization threshold that justifies buying vs leasing?

kevin: Rule of thumb we use: if utilization > 50% sustained for 9+ months, buying tends to win after factoring TCO and resale. For short spikes or uncertain demand, lease. Need exact TCO worksheets; I'll run a model if you give me expected month-by-month GPU-hours.

noah: Technical constraints for buying: PDUs/cooling in our us-west cage are near capacity — adding 100 nodes will require a second cage or colo expansion. That means additional monthly cross-connect + colo fees (~$12k/mo). Factor that into TCO.

procurement-bot: Purchase request template available: /templates/hardware-purchase-v2 — includes vendor SLA checklist and RMA expectations.

alex: Quick sensitivity calc I ran (very rough):
- Lease 12-week: ~120 nodes * $7k/mo/node * 3 months ~= $2.5M (covers peak)
- Buy 100 nodes capex: ~$6M upfront, spread depreciation gives cheaper monthly equivalent after 9-12 months.
So hybrid keeps runway.

maria: Sounds like we have a working plan. Action items:
- @kevin: model detailed 6/12/24 month TCO with colo fees (deadline Wed)
- @noah: confirm rack + network expansion cost and lead time (deadline Tue)
- @procurement-bot / procurement team: start vendor outreach for 12-week lease quotes and 6-9 month purchase quotes (deadline Fri)
- @alex: finalize peak GPU-hours by EOD today so finance can run numbers

sasha: +1 on hybrid. Also let's add a fallback policy: if observed Gen traffic < 70% of forecast by week 2 of the campaign, de-escalate additional lease capacity.

maria: Great — will consolidate into a single slide for leadership sync tomorrow. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
